cds.title: University of South Florida Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF)

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for the full 2026-27 year from the Common Data Set (G1). Tuition $4,559 in-state (printed on the in-district line; the in-state out-of-district line is blank) and $16,565 out-of-state/nonresident; required fees $1,851; on-campus food and housing $14,824 (housing $9,224 + meal plan $5,600). Estimated expenses (G5, residents): books $780, transportation $2,176, other $2,944 (other costs shown = transportation + other). Institutional aid for nonresidents is non-need-based only (CDS H6): 1,187 degree-seeking undergraduate nonresidents received it, average $10,001 (total $11,871,060).

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class): 71,722 applied, 29,196 admitted (40.7%), 6,730 enrolled; the residency rows (in-state / out-of-state / international) and the men + women rows both add up to the totals. International first-years: the CDS C1 residency rows print 559 applied, 493 admitted and 487 enrolled (international), but they cannot be used as an international admit rate: 487 of 493 admitted would be a 98.8% yield, in-state shows 5,484 of 5,533 enrolled (99%), the CDS B2 row for first-time first-year nonresidents says 467, and the 2024-25 CDS shows the same pattern (594 / 534 / 524). International applicants and admits are therefore left empty (null) rather than shown as 88.2%. The in-state and out-of-state counts are printed as in the CDS and should be read with the same caution; the gender rows and the overall totals are consistent with each other. Out-of-state applicants are the large majority (63,880) with a 36.3% admit rate versus 76.0% in-state. The CDS fills in no waitlist counts and no early-action counts, although USF's site lists Early Action and a waitlist as a Regular Decision outcome. Average GPA above 4.0 means USF reports a recalculated/weighted GPA; the GPA table is the 'all enrolled students' column (rows add to 99.98%) and 99.9% of enrollees had a GPA reported. Test submission is the share of enrolled first-years: 77.8% SAT, 21.7% ACT (C9). Undergraduate enrollment (39,093) and the nonresident count (2,913) are the 'Total Undergraduates' figures (they include non-degree-seeking students such as dual enrollment). Class rank: 29.1% in the top tenth, 62.8% in the top quarter (71.6% reported rank).
